### Observed differences

- Activity A01 was completely absent in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces) and appears in the later window exactly once in every trace (200 of 200, mean 1.0 occurrence per trace, never repeated within a case) [OCC001].
- In the earlier window, A03 was the closing event of every case: it occurred in all 200 traces at the final relative position (1.0 in every case) and showed no observed outgoing transitions. In the later window, A03 sits earlier in the trace (mean relative position about 0.86) and all 200 of its observed outgoing transitions lead to A01 [POS002, DIR002].
- The A01–A03 relationship changed accordingly: in the earlier window, 100 in 100 traces contained A03 without A01; in the later window, 100 in 100 traces contain both activities, always with A03 executed before A01 and no interleaving or repetition [REL001].
- In the later window, A01 always occupies the final position of the trace, i.e., it acts as a new closing step [POS001].
- Smaller shifts: A11 participation rose from about 24 to 30 in 100 traces, A06 fell from about 26 to 21 in 100; after A06, the share of outgoing transitions to A10 dropped from about 25% to 14% while the share to A09 rose from about 4% to 17% (these shares rest on only about 51 and 42 outgoing transitions) [OCC006, OCC004, DIR005].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 was added as a new mandatory closing step at the end of the process: in the later window every case executes A01 exactly once, immediately after A03, which in the earlier window was the final activity of each case. The supporting signs are direct and consistent across indicator families: A01's participation went from 0 to 200 of 200 traces [OCC001]; A03 went from having no observed successors to leading to A01 in all 200 observed transitions [DIR002]; the A01–A03 relation changed from "A03 alone" to co-occurrence with A03 first in every trace [REL001]; and the positions match, with A03 moving off the final position and A01 taking it [POS001, POS002]. All of these items have empirical strength of about 0.995, though they describe one underlying trace behaviour and so corroborate rather than independently confirm each other. One limitation: zero participation in the earlier window strictly means only that A01 was not observed there, so an A01 that previously occurred extremely rarely cannot be fully excluded by these samples.

Other differences: the increased participation of A11 (48 to 60 of 200 traces) and decreased participation of A06 (51 to 42), together with the shifted transition shares after A06, are not part of this hypothesis; they are based on modest supports and moderate empirical strengths (about 0.7–0.8), and without a screening baseline the evidence cannot rule out that they are sampling variation.
